rows.scope: Chromium (hexavalent) — Table 64431-A Maximum Contaminant Levels, Inorganic Chemicals, 22 CCR §64431 ('Public water systems shall comply with the primary MCLs in Table 64431-A')
rows.basis: mg/L in drinking water delivered by public water systems; 0.010 mg/L = 10 µg/L (≈10 µg/kg for water)
rows.evidence: Chromium (hexavalent) 0.010 [mg/L] — Table 64431-A, §64431, held text p.2 of 17; LII: operative 10/1/2024
rows.primary_source_used: /Users/karenpendergrass/Desktop/heavy-metal-index/raw/regulatory/us-ca/ca-swrcb-hexavalent-chromium-mcl-regulation-text-2024.pdf (SWRCB-DDW-21-003 regulation text, Feb 2024) corroborated by https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/22-CCR-64431 (current CCR text: 'Amendment of section and NOTE filed 7-24-2024; operative 10/1/2024 (Register 2024, No. 30)') and https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/drinking_water/certlic/drinkingwater/Chromium6.html ('The hexavalent chromium MCL is 0.010 mg/L or 10 µg/L'; effective October 1, 2024)
rows.note: Packet gave no raw_paths, no register_urls and an empty row url; the held copy was found by searching raw/regulatory. The held copy is the PROPOSED regulation text (footer 'Regulation Text (proposed)'), so the value was re-confirmed against the current operative CCR text on LII, which is identical (Cr-VI 0.010 mg/L; total Cr 0.05 mg/L). Adopted by SWRCB 2024-04-17, operative 2024-10-01. Table 64432-B phases the compliance date by system size (proposed text: 2/3/4 years after effect; SWRCB materials: 2026-10-01 for ≥10,000 connections, 2027-10-01 for 1,000–9,999, 2028-10-01 for <1,000), so on 2026-09-02 the MCL is in force but no system's compliance date has yet arrived. The earlier 2014 DPH MCL of 10 µg/L was invalidated by Sacramento Superior Court in 2017 (economic feasibility) and withdrawn; the 2024 rule is the re-adoption. A web search on 2026-09-02 found no ruling invalidating the 2024 MCL. Lower-tier metadata suggestion (not a verdict factor): the register should carry the SWRCB Chromium6 page or 22 CCR §64431 as url, and the raw copy should be replaced or supplemented by the OAL-approved final text.

rows.basis: mg/Kg of the product as sampled; reg 30(2): non-compliant when any one sample unit exceeds the Schedule level; no wet/dry qualifier stated (row 'basis' field holds a unit string, not a basis)
rows.evidence: Muscle meat of fish, excluding those listed below. 0.2 (mg/Kg) — Eleventh Schedule A(15), PDF p.108
rows.primary_source_used: /Users/karenpendergrass/Desktop/heavy-metal-index/raw/regulatory/fj/fiji-food-safety-regulations-2009-chemical-contaminants.pdf (Legal Notice No. 20, Food Safety Regulations 2009, 201 pp)
rows.note: The row url and the packet register_url (https://biotech.law.lsu.edu/obesity/who/report_food_safety_consultation.pdf) is NOT the instrument: fetched and read, it is the WHO/FAO/SPC 'Pacific Islands Food Safety and Quality Consultation' report (Nadi, 11–15 Nov 2002; WPRO, Feb 2003; 59 pp) and contains no Eleventh Schedule or fish-lead table. The verdict rests on the held copy; a correct public url is https://www.health.gov.fj/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/33_The-Food-Safety-Regulations-2009.pdf (surfaced by search, not fetched). Reg 1(2): commences on Gazette publication; reg 30(1) applies the Eleventh Schedule limits to food imported into or produced/processed in Fiji. In the gazetted text the Schedule header reads 'FOOD SAFETY REGULATIONS 2008' and '(Regulation 28 (1))' although reg 30(1) is the operative cross-reference — typographical defects in the instrument itself. In-force status: InforMEA/FAOLEX shows 'Repealed: No' with amendments L.N. 89/2010 (Schedule 11: dioxins/PCBs in fisheries products; canned-food standards — lead not touched), L.N. 35/2014 (reg 22 nutrient labelling — Schedule not touched) and L.N. 19/2019 (scope not reachable: laws.gov.fj and LEAP returned 404/403); the consolidated laws.gov.fj text (DisplayAct/501) was also unreachable, so the possibility that the 2019 amendment altered para (15) could not be excluded from primary text. ECOLEX (LEX-FAOC110379 mirror) independently shows the 2009 Regulations not repealed and lists only the 2010 and 2014 amendments; FAOLEX itself returned 403. Listed-species exception row (bonito, horse mackerel/scad, sardine, sardinops, spotted seabass, tuna) = 0.4 mg/Kg; crustaceans excl. brown crab meat 0.5; cephalopods 1.0.
